items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: One night I had Al Belanco who is now a leader. He was playing second trumpet with me.

ctx.x: I don't like to talk. I don't have a stick. Sure. I'm curious to know about some of the other orchestras. How would you describe Robichaux and the kind of jobs, what kind of jobs did he get, do you know of, and Perrone? Well, as I told you, I was- You're so busy yourself.

I was so busy that I, but I used to tell Mr. Grimowall and Mr. Cobb that I would like to know what the others are doing. So I'd like a night off once in a while, you see? So I'd go out and see Perrone, and he knew me, and he was a crippling violinist. He wrote, I wish I could shimmy like my sister Kate, you know, and I don't know whether he got credit for it. And I would listen to the bands and see what they're doing, and perhaps if I didn't think it's good enough I wouldn't shimmy. Because my father always told…

I was curious to know if you felt that, actually, you did go around the country and other places. Yes. Did you feel that you were really ahead of the trends coming from New Orleans, that they discovered a lot of things just a lot later and picked them up, things that had been done a long time before here, like when you were a kid or just coming up in music.
